We need a CloudFormation template that creates the IAM roles, instance profiles, and managed policies required for the Cluster API Provider AWS to manage Kubernetes clusters, including both EC2-based and EKS-based cluster lifecycle. The template must define three instance profiles named "control-plane.cluster-api-provider-aws.sigs.k8s.io", "controllers.cluster-api-provider-aws.sigs.k8s.io", and "nodes.cluster-api-provider-aws.sigs.k8s.io", each associated with corresponding IAM roles. The roles should allow EC2 (and for controllers also pods.eks.amazonaws.com) to assume them, and include managed policies granting broad permissions for EC2, ELB, auto scaling, EKS, and other AWS services necessary for provisioning and managing VPCs, subnets, security groups, load balancers, auto scaling groups, and the EKS cluster itself. Additionally, the template must create a separate IAM role for the EKS control plane with the AmazonEKSClusterPolicy attached, and a node role with AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy and AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy. The policies should be scoped to the specific resource ARNs and aliases as required by the Cluster API, such as for secrets and service-linked roles. All resources should be named with the exact suffixes as in the standard Cluster API IAM conventions.

cfn_description: Sets up SecurityHub with a delegated administor and automatically enabled for all AWS accounts in the AWS Organization. (qs-1s3rsr7n9)
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a fully automated Security Hub deployment across our entire AWS Organization, leveraging AWS Control Tower. The solution should automatically enable Security Hub in the designated audit account as the delegated administrator, then enable Security Hub in the log archive account and any future accounts created via Control Tower, adding them as members. It must use EventBridge rules that react to the Control Tower lifecycle events indicating a new account was successfully provisioned and that the landing zone setup or update has finished, invoking SSM automation documents that handle the cross-account enablement, member invitation, and acceptance workflows. The automation should read the audit and log archive account IDs from configuration values stored under the "/superwerker/" path in Parameter Store, and should perform cross-account actions by assuming the cross-account administration role that AWS Control Tower automatically provisions in every account it manages, named "AWSControlTowerExecution". The template should define all required IAM roles, SSM documents, and EventBridge rules to make the process fully event-driven and self-service.

user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a fully automated failover solution for an Aurora Global Database using an SSM Automation document and a Lambda function. The template should set up the necessary IAM roles for both SSM and Lambda, giving the automation role enough access across RDS, Route 53 Application Recovery Controller, Secrets Manager, and Systems Manager to carry out a regional failover, and giving the Lambda role permission to start and check SSM automation executions. The SSM document, named AuroraGlobalDatabaseFailoverSSMDocument, should orchestrate a full failover of the Aurora Global Database cluster named aurora-global-test: it needs to work out which region is currently active by reading the ARC routing control values stored as SSM parameters under the /app-failover/ path (arc-control-us-east-1, arc-control-us-west-2, and arc-cluster), promote the standby region through a global cluster failover, update the ARC routing controls so they match the new active region, and keep the connection details in the aurora-failover-db-secret Secrets Manager secret current with the new writer endpoint. The Lambda function, named TriggerFailover, should be a simple HTTP-triggered function whose only job is to start this SSM automation execution. Assume the primary and secondary regions are us-east-1 and us-west-2 respectively, with the template itself deployed in us-east-1.

cfn_description: AnyCompany Hotel - Cognito User Pool for guest and staff authentication with email sign-in and custom guest_id attribute.
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Cognito user pool for AnyCompany Hotel's guest and staff authentication system, using the PLUS tier with advanced security features enforced, email as the username attribute, admin-only user creation, and custom attributes for guest_id, property_id, and region, along with a solid password policy and email-based account recovery; the stack should include a public SPA client using SRP auth with no secret and a separate dedicated admin auth client using ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD_AUTH for server-side test harnesses and simulators, both with 1-hour access/id tokens and 30-day refresh tokens, plus Cognito groups for Admin, Manager, RegionalManager, RevenueManager, FrontDesk, and Housekeeping staff roles, an M2M OAuth2 client with its own resource server and read/write/admin scopes using client_credentials flow with a secret, and a user pool domain name that includes the environment and account ID so the OAuth2 token endpoint is accessible; the environment parameter should default to dev and allow dev, staging, and prod, and all resources should export their IDs, ARN, client IDs, and the domain URL for cross-stack references.

cfn_description: Create Glue catalog tables for Neptune Athena Connector sample
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates Glue catalog databases and tables for querying a Neptune graph dataset via Athena, supporting both property graph and RDF models using the Neptune Athena connector. It must create two separate Glue databases, one for property graph tables and one for RDF tables, each with a default name of "graph-database" and "graph-database-rdf" respectively. Every table across both databases should use a comma as its field separator character. For the LPG database, include tables named airport, country, continent, route, and customairport, with the airport table having columns for id, type, code, icao, desc, region, runways, longest, elev, country, city, lat, and lon, the country and continent tables having id, code, and desc columns, the route table having id, out, in, and dist columns, and the customairport view needing a source and destination column. All columns should be typed as strings except for numeric fields, which should use an integer type for runways, longest, elev, and dist, and a double-precision floating point type for lat and lon. The airport, country, and continent tables should each be configured as a vertex-type table with a graph label matching their own table name (airport, country, and continent respectively). The route table should be configured as an edge-type table with a graph label of route. The customairport table should be configured as a view-type table. The customairport view uses the following exact Gremlin traversal query to select source and destination airport codes for up to 10 routes: "g.V().hasLabel(\"airport\").as(\"source\").out(\"route\").as(\"destination\").select(\"source\",\"destination\").by(\"code\").limit(10)". For the RDF database, include a table named airport_rdf with the same column structure and types as the LPG airport table, plus a classuri parameter set to "class:Airport", a prefix_class parameter pointing to http://kelvinlawrence.net/air-routes/class/, a prefix_prop parameter pointing to http://kelvinlawrence.net/air-routes/datatypeProperty/, a querymode of class, and this table should be marked as an rdf-type table with a subject setting of id, a predicate prefix setting of prop, and stripping of URI prefixes enabled (strip_uri true). Also include two route tables named route_rdf and route_rdf_nopfx, both with incode and outcode columns as strings and a dist column as an integer, a querymode of sparql, marked as rdf-type tables with stripping of URI prefixes enabled (strip_uri true). The route_rdf table uses a prefix_prop parameter pointing to http://kelvinlawrence.net/air-routes/datatypeProperty/ and a prefix_op parameter pointing to http://kelvinlawrence.net/air-routes/objectProperty/, with the following exact SPARQL query text for selecting route codes and distances: "select ?incode ?outcode ?dist where { ?resin op:route ?resout . GRAPH ?route { ?resin op:route ?resout } . ?route prop:dist ?dist . ?resin prop:code ?incode . ?resout prop:code ?outcode . }". The route_rdf_nopfx table uses the same prefix_prop and prefix_op parameters but embeds the prefix declarations directly inside the query text instead of relying on the separate parameters, using this exact query: "PREFIX prop: <http://kelvinlawrence.net/air-routes/datatypeProperty/> PREFIX op: <http://kelvinlawrence.net/air-routes/objectProperty/> select ?incode ?outcode ?dist where { ?resin op:route ?resout . GRAPH ?route { ?resin op:route ?resout } . ?route prop:dist ?dist . ?resin prop:code ?incode . ?resout prop:code ?outcode . }".

user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates four DynamoDB tables for the Plot Palette application: Jobs, Queue, Templates, and CostTracking. The Jobs table should have a hash key on job_id and a GSI on user_id with a range key on created_at, projected with all attributes. The Queue table should have a hash key on status and a range key on job_id_timestamp. The Templates table should have a hash key on template_id and a range key on version, with a GSI on user_id projecting all attributes. The CostTracking table should have a hash key on job_id and a range key on timestamp, with TTL enabled on the ttl attribute. All tables must use on-demand billing, server-side encryption with KMS, and point-in-time recovery. The template should include an EnvironmentName parameter with allowed values 'development', 'staging', 'production' defaulting to 'production', and table names should follow the pattern plot-palette-<TableName>-<Environment>. Outputs for each table name and ARN, as well as the GSI name, should be exported with the stack name as a prefix for cross-stack referencing.

user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a simple Lambda function for testing purposes, which returns a hello message along with git metadata (commit SHA and branch) from environment variables. The template should include parameters for GitSha, GitBranch, and GitRepo with default "unknown", as these are automatically injected by the trupositive deployment tool. The Lambda function should use Python 3.11 runtime with a 30-second timeout and inline code. It needs an IAM role with the AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole managed policy, and a CloudWatch log group with 7-day retention. All resources should be tagged with git_sha, git_branch, git_repo, and managed_by. The outputs should include the function name, ARN, a git metadata summary, and a sample test command.

user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a secure S3 backend for storing Terraform state files, including a DynamoDB table for state locking, an S3 bucket with versioning and KMS encryption enabled, and an IAM role for managing the state. The solution should include an optional CloudTrail trail to log data events on the state bucket with logs optionally sent to CloudWatch, a KMS key with automatic rotation for encrypting everything, and a supporting log archive bucket with lifecycle rules to move logs to Glacier after 30 days and delete them after 365 days, plus an object lock retention of 30 days on the log bucket. The admin IAM principal and an execution principal should each be configurable, defaulting to the current AWS account when left unset, with optional tag-based conditions for assuming the role that require a Repository tag matching a configurable value which itself defaults to the name parameter. The template needs to accept a name parameter that defaults to the AWS account ID, and must support an optional VPC ID restriction for S3 bucket access, as well as support for an optional SSO permission set ARN. Noncurrent versions of state files should be automatically purged after 90 days.

cfn_description: CloudWatch dashboard and metric filters for Claude CoWork (Claude Desktop) telemetry. Reads events from /aws/claude-cowork/events log group and extracts token/cost metrics.
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a CloudWatch dashboard and associated metric filters for monitoring Claude CoWork (Claude Desktop) telemetry, reading events from the /aws/claude-cowork/events log group to extract token usage and cost metrics. The template should handle two different event schemas: one where the body is "claude_code.api_request" with attributes like input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_creation_tokens, cost_usd, user_email, and model, and another where body.name is "lam_session_turn_completed" with attributes nested under body.attributes including input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, total_cost_usd, and user_email. For the "claude_code.api_request" schema, the metric filters should include dimensions for user_email and model, while the "lam_session_turn_completed" schema should use a DefaultValue of 0 instead of dimensions. All metrics should be published under the ClaudeCoWork namespace with metric names token.usage.input, token.usage.output, token.usage.cache_read, token.usage.cache_creation, cost.usage, and session.turns. The dashboard should include widgets for total tokens, total cost, session turns, cache hit tokens, time-series charts for token usage and cost over time, turns per hour, average cost per turn, per-user breakdowns for token usage, cost, and session turns, cost by model, active user count, and a raw log table of recent events. The dashboard name should be configurable via a parameter with a default of ClaudeCoWorkDashboard, and the region for metrics should also be parameterized with a default of us-east-1.

user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a content-level PII classification scanner for files exposed through an S3 Access Point, using Amazon Comprehend's DetectPiiEntities to identify sensitive data and storing the results in a DynamoDB table with optional SNS notifications. By default the scanner Lambda should run outside any VPC, which is the simplest path and only works if the access point being scanned is internet-origin; before invoking, the access point's NetworkOrigin should be checked (via the access point's describe/get call) and if it comes back as VPC-scoped, the VPC ID, subnet IDs, a security group ID, and route table IDs must be supplied so the Lambda can be deployed inside that same VPC to reach it, since these all default to empty for the outside-VPC case. When a VPC ID is supplied, the template should optionally create the VPC endpoints needed for the Lambda to reach S3, DynamoDB, Comprehend, and SNS, controlled by a create-endpoints flag that defaults to true; this flag should be set to false instead if the target VPC already has any of those four endpoints, since a duplicate Interface endpoint for a service that already has one, or a second S3 Gateway endpoint bound to the same route tables, will fail and roll back the whole stack. The template should include a DynamoDB table for classification reports with point-in-time recovery and encryption, an IAM role granting the Lambda permissions to read from the access point, call Comprehend, write to DynamoDB, publish to SNS, and create logs, and a Lambda function with configurable memory (defaulting to 512 MB), timeout (defaulting to 600 seconds), a default Comprehend language code (defaulting to English, i.e. 'en'), and a default maximum number of files to scan per invocation (defaulting to 500, as a cost and runtime control). The Lambda code should handle chunking of large files, sampling, and pagination through the access point's objects. The stack should output the scanner function ARN, the report table name, and an example CLI invocation command.
